cur:monumental-santa-prassede-zeno-lamb.summary: In a lunette framed by bands of ornament, the haloed Lamb of God stands on a green mountain from which the rivers of Paradise flow, while two harts approach from either side to drink. The image joins the Lamb of the Apocalypse with the deer of Psalm 42, which 'panteth after the water brooks', a familiar symbol of the soul longing for God.
facts: The Chapel of Saint Zeno was built by Pope Paschal I (817–824) as a funerary chapel for his mother, Theodora; its walls and vault are almost entirely clad in gold-ground mosaic.
Paschal I's mosaics belong to the Carolingian-era revival in Rome, when the pope also translated many martyrs' relics from the catacombs into the city's churches.
